findings.topic: Owned locale and explicit invalid-call policy
findings.observation: OwnedCrt creates an explicit nonempty NUL-free compiler locale with _create_locale, frees it at final ownership release, and compares through _stricmp_l/_wcsicmp_l. Null comparisons are handled before CRT entry. The owned returning/throwing invalid handler receives explicit operation/reason/error metadata; invalid copy clears valid output before notification. Returning handler sets compiler errno to EINVAL/ERANGE. Overlap and capacity above INT_MAX are excluded domains. No global/thread locale or invalid-handler setters are used. German and C comparisons, handler lifetime, NUL, capacity and untouched-tail checks support the selected policy, not original static CRT equivalence.

Resources and ByteWide retain the shared virtual CrtProvider; an owned-only ByteWide no longer requires unused legacy function pointers. Narrow and inherited final wide routes dispatch to that same provider. Legacy complete-table behavior remains available. Actual foreign factory copies retain handler context through consumption; native Context ownership releases it after explicit pause/close. Resources precedes ByteWide in Storage, so the wide frontend is destroyed before its backing Resources owner. No ownership cycle was found.

findings.topic: All four lower CRT checkpoint routes
findings.observation: The foreign factory wraps either selected owned CRT or complete legacy table using the same actual Domain permission as encoding. All four virtual operations check before and after the lower invocation, without a metadata mutex spanning provider calls. Checks separately preserve WinLastError. Valid exceptional postchecks rethrow the identical exception; invalid postcondition wins and prevents the next lower call. Manual actual-PTD integration verifies fresh scope cleanup after handled invalid-copy exception, and poisoned retention after handler FLS mutation.

findings.topic: Byte-safe bridge prefixes and exceptional error
findings.observation: ByteWide retains actual wchar_t staging and memcpy-only borrowed UTF16 access. Normal and throwing lower routes capture outgoing WinLastError before staging destruction. Actual output first unit remains cleared before a throwing invalid-copy handler while unused tail remains untouched. Staging and invalid-output preclear occur BEFORE the lower CRT checkpoint, as explicitly documented; this is not an effect-free guard at the entire wide bridge entry. No blind output rollback or provider retry was introduced.

NumericEncoding owns its lower Calls and immutable explicit selector plus validated numerical ANSI/OEM pages. It does not consult ambient compiler locale or AreFileApisANSI. Recovered helpers select 65001/0/1 and conversion flags first; only lower cp0/cp1 are resolved to explicit numeric pages. Other values pass through except ambient aliases2/3, which reject. UTF8 aliases do not silently receive UTF8-specific flags. Existing used-default, invalid-flags retry, counted NUL, query/fill length and tail/error behavior is retained. Native Win32 UTF8 and1252 conversions are tested. select constructs both replacements before mutation and documents prepublication use before foreign make_factory.

remaining_proof_obligations: Owned locale, handler and numerical encoding apply only when explicitly selected. Legacy/default CrtApi and NativeCalls remain ambient outside this selected path; no process-wide freezing is claimed.
Compiler locale, compiler errno and recovered PTD initial locale/errno domains remain distinct. No original static CRT layout, invalid-handler, debug-fill, exception ABI or DLL equivalence is proved.

Wide staging and invalid-output preclear precede lower CRT permission checks; a denied call is not guaranteed effect-free at the wide bridge entrance. Unreadable/non-NUL inputs, overlapping copies and capacities above INT_MAX remain excluded.

IsValidCodePage does not guarantee every retained flag combination is valid for every numeric page. Aliases resolving to UTF8 retain pre-resolution flags/used-default arguments and may return the original-style conversion error; no silent flag upgrade is performed.
Arbitrary provider/handler reentry, raw PTD free/ABA, temporary mutation restored between checks and inaccurate FLS getters remain outside the supported single-active domain.
